recentItems.title: Pinglu Canal opens in China’s Guangxi
recentItems.description:
Read more: https://sc.mp/ec963b

China’s new Pinglu Canal entered service as the country’s first river-to-sea canal on Wednesday. Built to handle ships of up to 5,000 tonnes, the infrastructure will shorten the transit distance from southwestern Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region to the sea by 560km (348 miles), bypassing ports in Guangdong province. By linking an expansive system of rivers and tributaries directly to the Gulf of Tonkin, the waterway provides landlocked areas across southern and southwestern China – such as Sichuan, Guizhou and Yunnan provinces – with faster routes to Asean markets and international sea lanes.

recentItems.title: Trump blames China for data centre anger in this American town
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Read more: https://sc.mp/49617e

In recent years, Loudoun County in the US state of Virginia has become known as the data centre capital of the world. The community of Sterling has even earned the name “data centre alley”, after around 250 data centres were built in the area only slightly larger than Hong Kong and plans were made for more than 100 more. About 75 per cent of Americans now oppose having data centres built near them, up from 42 per cent just a year ago, according to a poll published by Heatmap News. Residents have complained about noise and pollution caused by the booming AI industry. However, US politicians including President Donald Trump, as well as tech industry advocates, say Chinese influence campaigns are amplifying grassroots opposition – a claim locals who live near the centres deny.

recentItems.title: China pushes back against US claims of AI being ‘too powerful’
recentItems.description:
Read more: https://sc.mp/74b83f

Calls by US tech leaders for a voluntary slowdown in artificial intelligence development have prompted a sharp pushback from China. Researchers and state media have questioned whether the proposal is a genuine push for industry responsibility or an effort to entrench America’s technological lead. The response comes as major AI developers disclose cases of their AI agents breaking out of secure testing environments.

recentItems.title: The green balancing act of building Hong Kong airport’s third runway
recentItems.description:
In partnership with: Airport Authority Hong Kong

Hong Kong International Airport (HKIA) expanded its capacity with the three-runway system project, which included reclaiming 650 hectares (1,606 acres) of land over contaminated mud pits using pioneering and eco-friendly engineering solutions that would protect the surrounding waters. As a result, marine life has actually thrived around the new runway in response to some of the measures taken. 

Join Tommy Leung, executive director of engineering and technical services for the Airport Authority Hong Kong, and marine biologist Kenneth Leung as they tour HKIA and discuss how the development of the third runway set a new global standard for sustainable coastal infrastructure.

The construction work involved using deep cement mixing – a process that injects cement into soft mud to create solid foundation pillars – to avoid potential toxic releases from traditional dredging. The project also features structured eco-sea walls and artificial reefs that have oyster shells attached, which create crucial microhabitats that can double local marine biodiversity.

recentItems.title: Indonesian volunteers deliver oxygen tanks as wildfire haze worsens
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

In Indonesia’s West Kalimantan province, volunteers have been making door-to-door deliveries of oxygen tanks to residents who have breathing problems amid severe wildfire haze across the region. As Indonesia faces its worst wildfire season in 11 years, outreach teams have also set up oxygen stations to support firefighters battling hazardous conditions.
